chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Abi Hamza and al-Husayn ibn Yahya, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who gave a man money to perform Hajj on his behalf, and he died, he said: 'If he died in his house before departing, it does not suffice for him; and if he died on the road, it has sufficed for him.'
ai.seo_question: Does the agent's death invalidate the Hajj performed on behalf of the payer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the condition of 'exit from home' (khuruj min al-bayt) as the critical threshold for the validity of Hajj al-Badal, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining when the obligation transfers to the agent. It highlights the juristic principle that the agent's death during the journey signifies the completion of the requisite act, thereby fulfilling the payer's duty, whereas death prior to departure leaves the obligation unfulfilled.
